newsitem.title: USA: Chile purchases Palanca, Oriente crude for Dec.
newsitem.headline: Chile purchases Palanca, Oriente crude for Dec.

text.p: Chile's state oil company Empresa Nacional del Petroleo (ENAP) bought a cargo each of Angolan Palanca and Ecuadorian Oriente for December in its latest purchase tender, trade sources said Thursday.
ENAP bought about one million barrels of Palanca crude loading at the end of November, and about 400,000 barrels of Oriente loading in early December.

Market sources said Palanca was sold to the state firm by Elf Aquitaine at Dated Brent plus 25 cents a barrel fob, and Oriente was sold at an unknown price by Glencore, very likely at a discount to West Texas Intermediate.

"I'm quite sure ENAP bought the cargo based on WTI (West Texas Intermediate). They run more risk pricing off WTS (West Texas Sour/Midland), because of the (volatile) spread between WTI/WTS," a Latin American trader said.
Ecuador changed the pricing formula for Oriente crude last month, switching the benchmark from WTI to WTS/Midland.
The market has so far preferred to quote spot Oriente into the U.S. Gulf against WTI.
Chile's tender for 960,000 barrels of crude for December closed on Wednesday.
